key_insight: As the number of spectral channels grows at fixed bandwidth and thickness, inverse-designed spectral routers face a fundamental throughput penalty: more routing constraints demand more optical capacity, lowering best-case efficiency.
engineering_relevance: This quantifies the design trade-off for compact snapshot spectral imagers, helping engineers balance spectral resolution against detector throughput and device miniaturization.
method: Used delay-bandwidth analysis to relate channel count, efficiency, and thickness.
Designed TiO2/SiO2 spectral routers with adjoint-based topology optimization.
Verified performance with 3D finite-difference time-domain simulations for 9, 16, 25, and 36 channels.
evidence_signal: Across matched conditions, the maximum near-plateau routing efficiency decreased from 97.0% at 9 channels to 82.3% at 36 channels, while changing wavelength spacing or assignment altered efficiency by less than 1 percentage point.
watch_item: Results are tied to a specific material stack, fixed thickness, and visible-band setting, so broader performance may differ under other fabrication tolerances or optical constraints.
paper_title: Scaling Limits of Multichannel Spectral Routers for Snapshot Imaging
